cases.note: @locked is accepted only in the embedded tree, and every corpus case loads as a mounted domain, so no case here can load WITH it: the embedded tree's own locked rules (dsl/rules/rules.memql) are its positive, loaded by every boot. This is the nearest honest one -- the form the loader's refusal tells a bundle to write instead, an unlocked rule placed by @precedence.

cases.message: @locked is accepted only in the embedded tree
cases.note: A mounted rule that could lock itself would evaluate before every shipped rule; the rule loader refuses it by the tree it came from, which the parser cannot see.
